story.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgentSight is a local-first \u003ccode\u003etop\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003estrace\u003c/code\u003e-like observability tool for AI agents. It connects prompts, model calls, and tool decisions to their real effects on your machine.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSee what the agent is doing now.\u003c/strong\u003e Monitor active sessions, processes, resource, model and tool calls, file and network activity.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUnderstand failures and improve agent behavior.\u003c/strong\u003e Connect prompts and skills to errors, then turn them into better instructions and skills.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFind where time, tokens, and resources go.\u003c/strong\u003e Spot slow steps, retry loops, repeated model or tool calls, token-heavy sessions, and resource-hungry processes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAudit data movement and security-sensitive effects.\u003c/strong\u003e See which services received requests, which files changed, and whether agents stayed and give safety/security suggestions.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUse it with your existing agents.\u003c/strong\u003e Run AgentSight around Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw, or any command—without an SDK, proxy, or vendor integration.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNo SDK, no proxy, no vendor integration. \u003ccode\u003etop\u003c/code\u003e uses live eBPF process capture when you run it with sudo or your user already has passwordless/cached sudo. Without eBPF privileges, it falls back to process snapshots and native agent session files. With \u003ccode\u003erecord -- \u0026lt;command\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e, the monitored agent still runs as your normal user; only the probes are elevated.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQ: What's the performance impact?\u003c/strong\u003e\nA: Our evaluation reports less than 3% CPU overhead for typical traced agent workloads.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQ: Where does captured data go?\u003c/strong\u003e\nA: \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e stores sessions as \u003ccode\u003eagentsight-*.db\u003c/code\u003e files in the current directory by default, and \u003ccode\u003ereport\u003c/code\u003e reads the latest matching file from that directory unless you pass \u003ccode\u003e--db\u003c/code\u003e. When no default DB exists, report commands warn and fall back to local Claude/Codex/Gemini agent sessions where available. \u003ccode\u003emonitor\u003c/code\u003e stores its weekly background DBs under \u003ccode\u003e~/.agentsight/monitor\u003c/code\u003e, while \u003ccode\u003etop\u003c/code\u003e only shows live sessions. Use \u003ccode\u003eagentsight report\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eagentsight report list\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eagentsight report audit --json\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eagentsight report token\u003c/code\u003e to inspect prior runs. Captured data can include prompts, responses, paths, headers, and network targets, so treat logs and DBs as sensitive.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQ: Why doesn't AgentSight capture traffic from Claude Code, Node.js, or Gemini CLI?\u003c/strong\u003e\nA: These applications statically link their SSL library (BoringSSL for Claude/Bun, OpenSSL for \u003cstrong\u003eall\u003c/strong\u003e Node.js — both NVM and system installs) into their own binary instead of using system \u003ccode\u003elibssl.so\u003c/code\u003e, so there's nothing for sslsniff to hook by default. AgentSight handles this for you: \u003ccode\u003erecord -- \u0026lt;command\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e always discovers the binary, and \u003ccode\u003erecord -c node\u003c/code\u003e now auto-discovers the Node binary too. For Claude attach mode, pass \u003ccode\u003e--binary-path\u003c/code\u003e. See the \"Zero-Config: record\" and \"Monitoring Node.js AI Tools\" sections.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQ: Can AgentSight trace IDE agents like Cursor?\u003c/strong\u003e\nA: Not through eBPF. They are Electron apps that mostly run on macOS or Windows, their TLS sits inside a stripped framework binary and a helper process, and Cursor's API traffic is protobuf rather than JSON, so even a successful capture produces no LLM events. Support for these agents goes through the agent-native session path instead. See \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/master/docs/agents.md#ide-based-agents-cursor-antigravity-windsurf\"\u003eIDE-Based Agents\u003c/a\u003e for the details.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQ: What should I check if tracing fails?\u003c/strong\u003e\nA: Verify you are on Linux with eBPF support, have \u003ccode\u003esudo\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eCAP_BPF\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eCAP_SYS_ADMIN\u003c/code\u003e, and are using \u003ccode\u003erecord -- \u0026lt;command\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e or the correct \u003ccode\u003e--binary-path\u003c/code\u003e for statically linked agents.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e🤝 Contributing\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content--contributing\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 🤝 Contributing\" href=\"#-contributing\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWe welcome contributions! <p dir="auto">AI agents can run commands, rewrite files, spawn processes, and contact remote services—but when a run fails, stalls, or behaves unexpectedly, their logs rarely tell the whole story.</p>
<p dir="auto">AgentSight is a local-first <code>top</code>/<code>strace</code>-like observability tool for AI agents. It connects prompts, model calls, and tool decisions to their real effects on your machine.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>See what the agent is doing now.</strong> Monitor active sessions, processes, resource, model and tool calls, file and network activity.</li>
<li><strong>Understand failures and improve agent behavior.</strong> Connect prompts and skills to errors, then turn them into better instructions and skills.</li>
<li><strong>Find where time, tokens, and resources go.</strong> Spot slow steps, retry loops, repeated model or tool calls, token-heavy sessions, and resource-hungry processes.</li>
<li><strong>Audit data movement and security-sensitive effects.</strong> See which services received requests, which files changed, and whether agents stayed and give safety/security suggestions.</li>
<li><strong>Use it with your existing agents.</strong> Run AgentSight around Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw, or any command—without an SDK, proxy, or vendor integration.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">No SDK, no proxy, no vendor integration. AgentSight observes with eBPF and TLS traffic tracing, so it works even when the agent is a
closed-source CLI. <strong>✨ Zero SDK Required</strong></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Traditional Observability vs. System-Level Monitoring</h3><a id="user-content-traditional-observability-vs-system-level-monitoring" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Traditional Observability vs. System-Level Monitoring" href="#traditional-observability-vs-system-level-monitoring"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Application-level tools such as <a href="https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts" rel="nofollow">LangSmith</a>, <a href="https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview" rel="nofollow">Langfuse</a>, and <a href="https://arize.com/docs/phoenix/" rel="nofollow">Phoenix</a> are great for traces, prompts, tokens, evals, and latency when you own the application code. Gateway/proxy tools such as <a href="https://docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/integration-method/gateway" rel="nofollow">Helicone</a> are useful when you can route provider traffic through a managed endpoint.</p>
<p dir="auto">AgentSight focuses on the layer those tools often miss: what the agent actually does at the system boundary. It observes existing binaries and CLI agents without SDKs or proxies, then correlates LLM traffic with process execution, file access, and system activity.</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><strong>Challenge</strong></th>
<th><strong>Application-Level Tools</strong></th>
<th><strong>AgentSight Solution</strong></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Framework Adoption</strong></td>
<td>❌ SDK, callback, or gateway integration per app</td>
<td>✅ Drop-in system tracer, no code changes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Closed-Source CLIs</strong></td>
<td>❌ Limited to what the tool exposes or logs</td>
<td>✅ Observes existing binaries and CLI agents from outside</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Agent-Controlled Logs</strong></td>
<td>❌ Logs can be incomplete, disabled, or modified</td>
<td>✅ Kernel-level events independent of app logging</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>TLS LLM Traffic</strong></td>
<td>❌ Visible when routed through SDKs/proxies</td>
<td>✅ Captures plaintext at SSL/TLS calls without a proxy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>System Actions</strong></td>
<td>❌ Often misses subprocesses and local file activity</td>
<td>✅ Tracks process execution, file access, and resource use</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Cross-Boundary Behavior</strong></td>
<td>❌ Traces usually stop at framework/process boundaries</td>
<td>✅ Correlates LLM traffic with process and file events</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">AgentSight captures critical interactions that application-level tools miss:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Subprocess executions that bypass instrumentation</li>
<li>Plaintext LLM payloads at SSL/TLS call boundaries</li>
<li>File operations and system resource access</li>
<li>Cross-boundary behavior across LLM, process, and file events</li>
</ul>

<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Windows, macOS, or Linux</strong>: <code>top</code>, <code>bind</code>, <code>vis</code>, and <code>report</code> can use
agent-native session files without eBPF</li>
<li><strong>Linux kernel</strong>: 4.1+ with eBPF support (5.0+ recommended) for <code>record</code> and
the eBPF-backed debug commands</li>
<li><strong>sudo access on Linux</strong>: optional for <code>top</code>; eBPF is enabled automatically
when sudo is already available</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For source builds, see <a href="https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/master/docs/build.md">docs/build.md</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Rust Library</h3><a id="user-content-rust-library" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Rust Library" href="#rust-library"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Rust applications can depend on
<a href="https://crates.io/crates/agentsight-capture" rel="nofollow"><code>agentsight-capture</code></a> to reuse the

the <code>agentsight</code> package and is the library's primary consumer.</p>

<p dir="auto">For local use, install with <code>cargo install agentsight</code> or download the latest
release binary, then start with <code>agentsight top</code>. Use the examples below when
you want to record a specific command or inspect saved sessions.</p>
<p dir="auto">GitHub releases provide <code>agentsight-x86_64</code> and <code>agentsight-aarch64</code> for Linux.
The unsuffixed <code>agentsight</code> asset remains an x86_64 compatibility alias.
Native Windows builds are exercised by the Windows CI workflow; until a Windows
release asset is published, download its <code>agentsight-windows-x86_64</code> artifact or
build the collector crate from source.</p>
<p dir="auto">For Linux and Windows installation, background monitoring, Node binding,
automatic startup, upgrades, and removal, see
<a href="/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/master/docs/installation.md">Installation and Automatic Startup</a>.</p>

Codex, and Gemini sessions without sudo, then writes an animated replay to
<code>output/agent-nebula.gif</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cd your-repository
agentsight vis"><pre><span class="pl-c1">cd</span> your-repository
agentsight vis</pre></div>

<code>agentsight vis -o output/agent-nebula.html</code> for a self-contained HTML artifact

<p dir="auto">Every <code>record</code> session is automatically saved to an <code>agentsight-*.db</code> SQLite

<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: What permissions does AgentSight need?</strong>
A: <code>top</code> uses live eBPF process capture when you run it with sudo or your user already has passwordless/cached sudo. Without eBPF privileges, it falls back to process snapshots and native agent session files. With <code>record -- <command></code>, the monitored agent still runs as your normal user; only the probes are elevated.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: What's the performance impact?</strong>
A: Our evaluation reports less than 3% CPU overhead for typical traced agent workloads.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: Where does captured data go?</strong>
A: <code>record</code> stores sessions as <code>agentsight-*.db</code> files in the current directory by default, and <code>report</code> reads the latest matching file from that directory unless you pass <code>--db</code>. When no default DB exists, report commands warn and fall back to local Claude/Codex/Gemini agent sessions where available. <code>monitor</code> stores its weekly background DBs under <code>~/.agentsight/monitor</code>, while <code>top</code> only shows live sessions. Use <code>agentsight report</code>, <code>agentsight report list</code>, <code>agentsight report audit --json</code>, and <code>agentsight report token</code> to inspect prior runs. Captured data can include prompts, responses, paths, headers, and network targets, so treat logs and DBs as sensitive.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: Why doesn't AgentSight capture traffic from Claude Code, Node.js, or Gemini CLI?</strong>
A: These applications statically link their SSL library (BoringSSL for Claude/Bun, OpenSSL for <strong>all</strong> Node.js — both NVM and system installs) into their own binary instead of using system <code>libssl.so</code>, so there's nothing for sslsniff to hook by default. AgentSight handles this for you: <code>record -- <command></code> always discovers the binary, and <code>record -c node</code> now auto-discovers the Node binary too. For Claude attach mode, pass <code>--binary-path</code>. See the "Zero-Config: record" and "Monitoring Node.js AI Tools" sections.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: Can AgentSight trace IDE agents like Cursor?</strong>
A: Not through eBPF. They are Electron apps that mostly run on macOS or Windows, their TLS sits inside a stripped framework binary and a helper process, and Cursor's API traffic is protobuf rather than JSON, so even a successful capture produces no LLM events. Support for these agents goes through the agent-native session path instead. See <a href="https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/master/docs/agents.md#ide-based-agents-cursor-antigravity-windsurf">IDE-Based Agents</a> for the details.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Q: What should I check if tracing fails?</strong>
A: Verify you are on Linux with eBPF support, have <code>sudo</code> or <code>CAP_BPF</code>/<code>CAP_SYS_ADMIN</code>, and are using <code>record -- <command></code> or the correct <code>--binary-path</code> for statically linked agents.</p>
